title: Choose the visual world for the new GIP website
question: The roll assigned Survey Layers. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Survey Layers
options.lineage: GIS and cadastral maps: satellite imagery with vector layers, the view every buyer opens to check land
options.thesis: The site is a live map: aerial imagery, then the approved plan registered on top, then each plot's status, one layer per section.
options.viewport: Full-bleed aerial film framed as a map viewport: crosshair on the site, live lat/long, scale bar; huge headline; one scroll draws the 288-plot plan onto the land and fills it with live status beside WhatsApp and See the plan.
options.risk: Can turn cold or dashboard-like for families if the imagery and type are not warm and the chrome is not edited hard.

raised.raise: Two-tone discipline: chrome is only white and navy-black; colour appears only as data (plot status) or imagery.
Selecting a plot isolates it and dims every other layer; status is also written in line weight, never colour alone.
Orthogonal leader lines tie every fact (road width, approval, amenity) to its exact place on the map.
One shared pictogram set (gate, park, pool, tank, road) drawn in the map's line grammar, reused on every page.
One gesture deploys the whole plan: a single scroll registers the vector layer, stepped on phones.
Depth only by overlapping flat layers: no drop shadows, gradients or glass anywhere.

options.label: The Sales-Office Maquette
options.lineage: white architectural site models under glass at launch events
options.thesis: The layout as a white scale model you fly over: available plots stand proud, sold plots sit flush.
options.viewport: A WebGL white maquette extruded from the real 288-plot geometry, camera slowly orbiting under a soft studio light, headline over the open sky of the board.
options.risk: The most familiar idea for a developer (every sales office has the model), and WebGL weight on low-end Android.

options.label: Deployable Layout Sheet
options.lineage: Miura-fold sheet unfolding from a hand-sized packet
options.thesis: The layout copy as a folded packet that deploys into the full plan in one pull.
options.viewport: A gold packet on white that unfolds across the viewport into the 288-plot plan.
options.case: Fuses neatly with the folded layout copy, but loses to the map on both axes: buyers check land on satellite view, not origami.
options.kept: One gesture deploys the whole plan, stepped on phones.
options.risk: Origami reads as a design stunt rather than land.

options.label: Signal Wiring
options.lineage: Kraftwerk Man-Machine line diagrams on a traffic grid
options.thesis: Plot status as traffic signals wired to labels on a strict grid.
options.viewport: Black field, the plan as a wiring schematic, signals lighting available plots.
options.case: Status signals are clear, but the black schematic breaks the white brief and families do not see their land in it.
options.kept: Orthogonal leader lines tie every fact to its place on the map.
options.risk: Reads as a band poster, not a developer.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: 288 plots as a strobing black-and-white barcode field.
options.viewport: A wall of bars, one per plot, inverting as status changes.
options.case: Abstracts the land away; neither families nor NRIs recognise their plot in it.
options.kept: Total two-tone contrast discipline for chrome.
options.risk: Cold and unreadable for the audience.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: The layout as concentric detector rings with plots as tracks.
options.viewport: A dark ring section with the site at its centre.
options.case: Dark ground breaks the brief and the metaphor has nothing to do with buying land.
options.kept: Selection isolates one plot and dims the rest; weight encodes status.

options.label: Collective Plate
options.lineage: Toyism collective paintings with a shared symbol set
options.thesis: Every page painted from one shared symbol set.
options.viewport: Hovering symbols of gate, plot and tree on a flat ground.
options.case: Playful palette fights trust and the navy brand anchor.
options.kept: One shared pictogram set reused on every page.

options.label: Layered Papercut
options.thesis: Depth built from flat cut layers pasted one over another.
options.viewport: A symmetrical roundel of the layout built up in cut colour layers.
options.case: Beautiful craft, but folk ornament says nothing about approved land.
options.kept: Depth only by overlapping flat layers, never shadows or gradients.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A premium Hyderabad developer site executed impeccably: drone film, light serif headline, project cards.
canonCard.viewport: Full-bleed drone film with a large light serif headline and an Enquire pill, then project cards and amenity icons.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Honer and every competitor by design.
